ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A rose bush has 8 flowers on which butterflies and dragonflies are sitting. On every flower there is at most one insect sitting on it. More than half of the flowers are occupied. The number of butterflies is twice as big as the number of dragonflies. How many butterflies are sitting on the rose blossoms?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let D be the number of dragonflies and B be the number of butterflies. Since each flower has at most one insect, the total number of insects B + D equals the number of occupied flowers. There are 8 flowers, and more than half are occupied, so B + D > 4. Also, no more than 8 flowers can be occupied, so B + D <= 8. The problem says the number of butterflies is twice the number of dragonflies, so B = 2D. Therefore B + D = 2D + D = 3D. This means 4 < 3D <= 8. The only integer value of D that works is D = 2, since 3D = 6. Then B = 2D = 2 × 2 = 4.
